# Using SETTLE and KANERVA through settle-mcp

## Run a program

`run_program` takes a `path` to a `.settle` file or the program text as `source`, and returns what it printed, its errors and its exit code. Text runs in a fresh temporary folder.

`settle --version` prints the interpreter’s version; `check_system` asks the one setup built.

## When a program fails

A failing program exits with status 2. Its first line is `settle: line N: <message>`; under it the command prints the program line, a caret under the place, and its column. When a keyword, a thing or a statement is one letter off, the message ends with a suggestion, such as ``did you mean `leans:`?``.

Hand the whole printed error, caret line and all, to `explain_error`. It names the marked word, the suggested fix, the documented cause and its page, and a tested program that gives the same error.

## Start from a tested example

`list_examples` lists the tested programs from the SETTLE docs; `get_example` shows one with the exact output the interpreter is tested to print. Each is also a resource, `settle://examples/<name>`.

## Store and recall with a sparse distributed memory

`sdm_store_recall` writes named patterns, or short texts, into a sparse distributed memory and reads one back from a noisy read-address. It writes a short SETTLE program with the `sdm` statements, which call the KANERVA crate, and shows that program in its reply.

`address_noise` is the share of the read-address bits flipped before the read (default 0.2). A small address-noise comes back; near 0.4 the read stops finding the pattern, because the basins are narrow. `word_size` (bits per pattern, default 256) and `hard_locations` (default 2000) shape the memory. Reading a name that was never written shows the memory refusing.

The statement words it writes are read from the installed interpreter's `settle --help`, so the program always matches the SETTLE you built.

## Run a .kanerva program

A `.kanerva` program is written in SETTLE’s syntax and holds only the sdm family: `sdm`, `softsdm`, `sdmscale`, `refusal` and `contenttrack`, inside `model :name do ... end` and `run :name do ... end`. The `kanerva` command runs it on KANERVA alone, with no SETTLE, and prints the same lines `settle` prints for the same file.

`run_kanerva` runs one from a `path`, from `source`, or by `program` name (`sdm`, `softsdm`, `sdmscale`, `theory`), and says whether a named program printed its recorded output. The programs are resources too, `kanerva://programs/<name>`. One read only SETTLE runs: `via: :pulls`, which settles a SETTLE model, so `kanerva` refuses it by name.

`write-samples:` is the spelling of record for softsdm’s write samples; `write_samples:` still works.

## The same memory in Rust

The KANERVA crate has a Rails-style builder in `src/rails.rs` that speaks the same words: each statement is a type, each keyword a method of the same name with its hyphens turned into underscores, and printing an answer prints the line the file prints. `read_doc` with `kanerva://readme` shows it under "The Rails face"; `kanerva_quickstart` with `example` set to `rails` runs it.

## Refuse what was never stored

A read-address that was never written still comes back as something. KANERVA refuses it two ways: the travel rule (`refusal` in a program) and the calibrated refusal, which compares each read with reads from the memory’s own random probes and keeps working in a crowded store where the travel rule stops. `kanerva_quickstart` with `example` set to `calibrated_refusal` prints both on a light and a crowded store.

## Run KANERVA’s examples

`kanerva_quickstart` runs the crate's own example, `cargo run --release --example quickstart`, in the kanerva folder setup made; `example` picks another (calibrated_refusal, rails, sizing, capacity and the rest). Pass `dry_run` true to see the command without running it.

## Look a word up

`help` with a `topic` searches a glossary built from the site and its docs: statements, families, tokens, the words the docs define in bold, KANERVA modules, the site vocabulary, and KANERVA's terms file when it exists. The same list is the resource `settle-mcp://glossary`.
